<!-- pr-reviewer: 3ab6f4ae3fe36ca1eec3db77875b02064553422f -->
Ready for the maintainer to merge.

What looks good
- The whole record comes from the #4192 resolver (`milling_cutter::derive(..).assembled(base, nodes)`), so the multi-seat cutter gets kind, diameter, corner, flutes, flute length, centre cutting and the enclosed holder, and every seat plus the one-source law are checked at command-construction time.
- The insert's running data (tool material, cutting rows) is overlaid on the tool's own record on the single-seat path too, so one insert gives the same facts to each tool that cuts with it.
- `UpsertDocumentComponent::with_row` and `EditDocumentComponent::with_row` take the whole row, `EditDocumentComponent::new` keeps the held facts and running data, and the wrong-kind refusals (facts on a non-tool-item, running data on a non-insert) are made in the command door, before anything is applied.
- One undo step updates both tools from a shared insert; the operations go Stale through their stamps (no cascade write), and undo/redo restores the exact state (pinned by test).
- Refusals are named and whole: a seat that does not take the insert, `DC` off the seats, a fact on the wrong kind - all refused at construction with the component and the tool named, nothing changes.
- `tool_library_holders/multi_seat.rs` joins the existing `tool_library_holders` binary (no new top-level binary), and the decision file `docs/decisions/3646-multi-seat-record.md` records the app-slice design.

Results merged with main
- Trial merge against `origin/main` (903e420b3): clean, no conflict (the PR head's parent is that commit; already up to date).
- Local build and tests on the PR head (debug, worktree `.claude/worktrees/cc-pr4249-review`, `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=6 CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=6`):
  - `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test tool_library_holders`: 20 passed, 0 failed (includes the 4 new `multi_seat::` pinning tests).
  - `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib`: 318 passed, 0 failed.
  - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Author-reported (head 3ab6f4ae3, in the PR body): quick gate 42 steps, 0 failed; light lane 6 steps, 0 failed; clippy clean. Not re-run by me - the light lane is a release build that does not fit the review time box, and the diff is an app-layer change (no post/toolpath change, so the example catalog suites and heavy lanes are not owed; the issue is P6).

Targeted tests
- Pinning tests (this PR): `multi_seat::a_multi_seat_cutter_takes_its_whole_record_from_the_document`, `a_shared_insert_edit_updates_both_multi_seat_tools_in_one_undo_step`, `an_edit_that_breaks_a_seat_is_refused_by_the_tool_name`, `the_face_mill_is_refused_a_plunge_into_solid` - all 4 pass locally. The face-mill plunge refusal also pins that the derived record reads on the safety path (a non-centre-cutting face mill is refused a plunge into solid).
- No post or toolpath generator changed: no example catalog suite required.
- No heavy step: P6 (accepted enhancement), per the review rules.

Requested before merge
- Nothing blocking.

Questions / notes (not blocking)
- The two new fields are not in the project file yet (#3645 / PR #4233 owns that); the PR says so and both PRs must meet without losing either side.
- `row_law` checks running rows against `ToolKind::EndMill` as the milling representative. That is a deliberate choice (a milling tool never takes wire/torch/plasma/waterjet rows); a face mill gets the same check. Note only - the #3644 law shape is kept.
- The `row_law` fact check is `matches!(row.component.kind(), ComponentKind::ToolItem { .. })`, so a fact on a solid-tool item would be refused. Deliberate: cutter facts only on a cutter body.
- A `docs/decisions/` entry lists no new `camcraft-*` dependency (none was added), so the entry is right as is.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
